objectives: Trace astronomy from antiquity through the telescope era.
Identify the key empirical + theoretical breakthroughs of the 17th-18th centuries.
Summarize the 20th-century revolutions: extragalactic universe + radio astronomy.

slides.title: Ancient + medieval astronomy (Babylon to Tycho)
slides.body:
Astronomy is the oldest science — every settled civilization tracked the heavens for calendars, navigation, religion, agriculture. The data we have today builds on millennia of patient sky-watching.

**Babylonian astronomy (~1800 BCE - 100 CE)**: cuneiform records on clay tablets log eclipses, planetary motions (especially Venus), lunar phases. The **Saros cycle** (18 yr 11 d) for eclipse prediction was known. Babylonian sexagesimal (base-60) arithmetic gave us 360° in a circle, 60 minutes, 60 seconds.

**Greek astronomy (~500 BCE - 200 CE)**:
- **Aristotle (~350 BCE)**: geocentric cosmos with crystalline spheres; spherical Earth (from ship + lunar-eclipse shadow arguments).
- **Aristarchus of Samos (~280 BCE)**: first proposed a heliocentric model; estimated Sun-Earth + Moon-Earth distance ratios (geometrically correct method, wrong numbers).
- **Eratosthenes (~240 BCE)**: measured Earth's circumference from shadow lengths at Syene + Alexandria (~40000 km, within ~2% of modern).
- **Hipparchus (~150 BCE)**: greatest pre-modern observational astronomer. Compiled first comprehensive star catalog (~850 stars); invented magnitude scale; **discovered precession of the equinoxes (129 BCE)** by comparing his observations to those 150 yr earlier — the celestial pole drifts ~1°/72 yr (full cycle ~26000 yr).
- **Ptolemy (~150 CE)**: *Almagest* — the canonical geocentric synthesis with **epicycles + deferents + equants** to fit observed retrograde motions. Wrong cosmologically but predictively accurate; dominated astronomy for 1400 years. Also wrote *Geographia* + *Tetrabiblos* (astrology).

**Islamic Golden Age (~800-1400 CE)**: preserved + extended Greek astronomy. **Al-Battani**, **Al-Sufi** (deep-sky catalog including Andromeda 964 CE), **Al-Tusi** (Tusi couple — mathematical device later used by Copernicus), **Ibn al-Shatir** (14th c. Damascus — non-Ptolemaic planetary models). Maragha + Samarkand observatories produced precise tables (Ulugh Beg's Zij-i Sultani, 1437).

**Copernicus (1473-1543)**: Polish canon + astronomer. *De Revolutionibus Orbium Coelestium* (1543, published as he died) restored heliocentrism — Sun at center; Earth orbits, rotates daily. Still used circles + epicycles (no ellipses) so predictions weren't dramatically better than Ptolemy's; the revolution was conceptual + cosmological.

**Tycho Brahe (1546-1601)**: Danish nobleman; last great naked-eye observer. Built Uraniborg + Stjerneborg on the island of Hven; measured stellar + planetary positions to ~1 arcminute (4× better than predecessors). Recorded the 1572 supernova in Cassiopeia — proved 'fixed stars' do change, demolishing Aristotelian immutability. Tycho's hybrid model (planets orbit Sun, Sun orbits Earth) preserved geocentrism for theological reasons but was empirically equivalent to Copernicus for predictions.

slides.title: The scientific revolution: Kepler, Galileo, Newton
slides.body:
**Kepler (1571-1630)**: German mathematician; assistant + heir to Tycho. After Tycho's death (1601), Kepler inherited the Mars data. Eight years of calculation yielded the **three laws of planetary motion**:
1. **Law of ellipses** (*Astronomia Nova*, 1609): planets orbit the Sun in ellipses with the Sun at one focus.
2. **Law of equal areas** (1609): a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times — implying it moves faster at perihelion (closest to Sun).
3. **Harmonic law** (*Harmonices Mundi*, 1619): T² ∝ a³ (square of orbital period proportional to cube of semi-major axis).

Kepler also wrote on optics, dioptrics, snowflake symmetry, the *Somnium* (proto-science-fiction lunar voyage). Devoutly religious; sought 'harmony of the spheres' — found it not in music but in geometry. His mother was tried as a witch; he defended her successfully.

**Galileo (1564-1642)**: Italian polymath. In 1609 heard of the Dutch telescope (Lippershey 1608), built his own (3×, then 8×, then 30×), and pointed it at the sky. **Sidereus Nuncius (1610)** reported:
- Mountains + craters on the **Moon** (not a perfect sphere — Aristotle wrong).
- **Jovian moons** Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto (the Medicean stars) — visible mini-solar-system, refuting geocentrism.
- **Phases of Venus** (1610-11) — only possible if Venus orbits the Sun, killing pure Ptolemaic geocentrism.
- Sunspots (with Scheiner) — Sun rotates + is imperfect.
- The Milky Way resolved into countless stars.

His *Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems* (1632) defended Copernicanism; tried by Inquisition 1633, forced to recant, spent rest of life under house arrest. **The Galileo telescope inaugurated observational astronomy as we know it.**

**Newton (1642-1727)**: born the year Galileo died. **Principia Mathematica (1687)** unified terrestrial + celestial mechanics:
- Three laws of motion.
- **Universal gravitation**: F = G·m₁·m₂/r² — apple + Moon obey the same law.
- Derived Kepler's three laws from gravitation + dynamics.
- Solved the two-body problem; framed (but did not solve) the three-body problem.
- Invented the reflecting telescope (1668) — eliminating chromatic aberration of refractors.

Newton turned astronomy from a descriptive into a predictive physical science. Halley used Newton's mechanics to predict the 1758 return of his namesake comet (last seen 1682) — first dramatic predictive success of celestial mechanics.

slides.title: From Herschel to Hubble: discovering the universe
slides.body:
**William Herschel (1738-1822)**: German-born British musician turned astronomer. Built progressively larger reflectors (12-inch, 18.7-inch, 40-foot reflector 1789). Discoveries:
- **Uranus (13 March 1781)** — first new planet since antiquity; doubled the size of the known solar system.
- Two moons of Uranus (Titania + Oberon, 1787); two more of Saturn (Mimas + Enceladus, 1789).
- Infrared radiation (1800) — measured temperature beyond the red end of the solar spectrum.
- Cataloged 2500+ nebulae + star clusters with sister **Caroline Herschel** (first salaried female astronomer).
- Proposed the Milky Way had a flattened disk shape from star counts.

**Neptune (1846)**: predicted by **Urbain Le Verrier** (Paris) + **John Couch Adams** (Cambridge) independently from anomalies in Uranus's orbit. **Johann Galle** at Berlin Observatory pointed his telescope where Le Verrier said + found Neptune within an hour (23 Sept 1846). **First triumph of theoretical astronomy** — a new planet predicted by Newtonian gravity alone.

**Friedrich Bessel (1838)**: first reliable **stellar parallax** — 61 Cygni at 10.3 light-years (modern value 11.4 ly). Direct geometric proof of vast stellar distances. Henderson + Struve independently measured α Centauri + Vega around the same time. Parsec defined: 1 pc = distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond ≈ 3.26 ly.

**Spectroscopy enters astronomy (mid-1800s)**: **Fraunhofer (1814)** mapped dark absorption lines in solar spectrum; **Bunsen + Kirchhoff (1859)** identified them with chemical elements — astronomers could now read compositions + velocities of stars. Birth of astrophysics. **Huggins (1864)** + **Secchi (1860s)** classified stellar spectra; **Pickering + Cannon** at Harvard (~1890-1920) built the OBAFGKM sequence on 250000 stars.

**Henrietta Leavitt (1868-1921)**: Harvard 'computer'. Studied Cepheid variables in the Small Magellanic Cloud (1908). Found **Cepheid period-luminosity relation**: longer-period Cepheids are intrinsically brighter (a 'standard candle'). This made Cepheids the first reliable extragalactic distance indicator.

**Harlow Shapley (1885-1972)**: used Leavitt's Cepheids on globular clusters to map the **Milky Way**. Found Sun is NOT at the galactic center; we're ~25000 ly from a center in Sagittarius. Overestimated MW size (~300000 ly), thought all 'nebulae' were within it (1920 Shapley-Curtis 'Great Debate').

**Edwin Hubble (1889-1953)**: at Mt Wilson (100-inch Hooker telescope). **1923-24**: resolved Cepheid variables in the **'Andromeda Nebula' (M31)** — distance ~900000 ly (modern: 2.5 Mly). **Andromeda is a separate galaxy.** The universe is vastly larger than the Milky Way. **1929**: 24 galaxies + their Cepheid distances + recession velocities (from Slipher's spectra) → Hubble's law **v = H₀·d** — universe is expanding. The cosmological era begins.

**Karl Jansky (1932)**: Bell Labs engineer; found radio static from the Milky Way center while investigating shortwave interference. **Birth of radio astronomy.** **Grote Reber** (1937) built first dedicated radio telescope in his Illinois backyard; mapped the radio sky. WWII radar work + the post-war boom (Cambridge, CSIRO, Jodrell Bank) made radio a routine astronomical window — leading to quasars (1963), pulsars (1967), CMB (1965), and modern interferometric arrays.

question.question: Derive Kepler's third law from Newton's gravitation (circular case)
question.goal: Show that for a circular orbit of radius a, period T satisfies T² = (4π²/GM)·a³ — Kepler's third law with the Newtonian constant.

steps.prompt: Set centripetal acceleration v²/r equal to gravitational acceleration GM/r². Solve for v.
steps.reveal: m·v²/r = G·M·m/r² → v² = GM/r → v = √(GM/r). Orbital speed decreases with distance (Mercury fastest, Neptune slowest).

steps.prompt: Orbital period T = circumference / speed = 2π r / v. Express T².

acceptedAnswers: T = 2π r / √(GM/r) = 2π √(r³/GM), so T² = 4π² r³ / GM

steps.reveal: T = 2π r / v = 2π r / √(GM/r) = 2π √(r³/GM). Squaring: T² = 4π² r³/(GM). This is Kepler's third law with the constant 4π²/(GM).

steps.prompt: For the Sun-Earth system (Earth at 1 AU, T = 1 yr), check the constant.

acceptedAnswers: T² = (3.156×10⁷)² ≈ 9.96×10¹⁴ s²; a³ = (1.496×10¹¹)³ ≈ 3.35×10³³ m³; ratio T²/a³ = 4π²/(GM☉) ≈ 2.97×10⁻¹⁹ s²/m³ — matches GM☉ = 1.33×10²⁰ m³/s²

steps.reveal: T² = (3.156×10⁷ s)² ≈ 9.96×10¹⁴ s²; a³ = (1.496×10¹¹ m)³ ≈ 3.35×10³³ m³; T²/a³ ≈ 2.97×10⁻¹⁹ s²/m³ = 4π²/(GM☉) with GM☉ = 1.327×10²⁰ m³/s² — checks. Kepler's empirical law (1619) emerges from Newton's inverse-square gravitation (1687).

steps.prompt: Why does this method weigh the Sun? Generalize.

acceptedAnswers: Measure T + a for any orbiting body, solve M = 4π² a³ / (GT²) — gives the central mass

steps.reveal: M = 4π²a³/(GT²). Used to weigh: the Sun (planetary orbits), planets (moon orbits — Jupiter from Galilean moons, Earth from Moon), stars (binary orbits → stellar mass-luminosity relation), black holes (S-star orbits at galactic center — Genzel + Ghez Nobel 2020), galaxies (rotation curves, stellar streams). This single equation is the fundamental cosmic scale that emerged from the Kepler-Newton synthesis.

question.question: Why was Hubble's 1923-24 resolution of Cepheid variables in the Andromeda Nebula such a watershed result?
options: It proved the universe is expanding.

Cepheid period-luminosity (Leavitt 1908) gave reliable extragalactic distances; Hubble's measurement put Andromeda at ~900000 ly — far outside the Milky Way — settling the Shapley-Curtis 1920 Great Debate in favor of an extragalactic universe.
It detected the cosmic microwave background.
It proved Einstein's general relativity correct.
question.explanation: Hubble used Leavitt's Cepheid period-luminosity relation (1908) to measure Andromeda's distance as ~900000 ly (modern: 2.5 Mly) — vastly outside Shapley's estimate of Milky Way size (~300000 ly). 'Spiral nebulae' were external galaxies, not gas clouds within ours. The 1920 Shapley-Curtis Great Debate at the Smithsonian had divided astronomers; Hubble's measurement decisively confirmed Curtis's 'island universes'. The 1929 v = H₀·d expansion result came later + built on this. The Cepheid resolution made extragalactic astronomy + cosmology possible. Without distance, no cosmological inference is possible.

hints: What scale question did it answer?
slides.workedSolution: Hubble's 1923-24 Cepheid measurement of Andromeda (~900000 ly) decisively placed it outside the Milky Way (Shapley ~300000 ly). This settled the 1920 Shapley-Curtis Great Debate: spiral nebulae are external galaxies, not internal MW gas clouds. The extragalactic universe + cosmology become possible. Hubble's 1929 v = H₀·d law builds on this foundation.

question.question: In 1845, anomalies in Uranus's orbit could not be explained by known gravity. Within months, both Le Verrier (Paris) + Adams (Cambridge) predicted an unseen planet's position from gravitational perturbation; Galle (Berlin) found Neptune on 23 Sept 1846.
question.prompt: Walk through the methodology: (1) what observed quantity needed explanation; (2) how Newtonian gravity + perturbation theory framed the hypothesis; (3) why this was the first triumph of 'theoretical astronomy'; (4) contrast with the failed Vulcan hypothesis (Le Verrier predicted an inner planet to explain Mercury's perihelion advance — turned out to be a relativistic effect, Einstein 1915). What does this teach about model + anomaly + alternative explanations?

question.question: Write Hipparchus's discovery: the rate of precession of the equinoxes in degrees per year (modern value).

slides.workedSolution: Modern precession rate: 50.29 arcsec/yr ≈ 1°/72 yr ≈ 0.01388°/yr; full cycle 25772 yr. Hipparchus (129 BCE) detected it by comparing his stellar positions to those of Timocharis (~150 yr earlier). The pole star changes over millennia — Thuban (α Draconis) was the pole ~3000 BCE; Polaris now; Vega in ~12000 CE.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why the Galileo-Kepler-Newton synthesis (1609-1687) is considered the founding moment of modern observational + theoretical astronomy.
question.rubric: Mentions: Galileo 1609-10 turned the telescope to the sky — found Jovian moons (mini-solar-system), Venus phases (heliocentric proof), lunar mountains, sunspots, resolved Milky Way. Kepler 1609-1619 mined Tycho's precise Mars data → three laws (ellipses + equal areas + T² ∝ a³). Newton 1687 Principia unified celestial + terrestrial physics via F = GMm/r², derived Kepler's laws from gravitation, invented reflecting telescope. Together: empirical observation (Galileo) + mathematical regularity (Kepler) + physical theory (Newton). Astronomy became a predictive physical science — Halley 1758 comet return, Le Verrier 1846 Neptune. This 70-year arc set the template for all subsequent astrophysics — observe carefully, find patterns, derive from underlying physics.
